instruction: Add the presenter note 'No content slide.' to slide 7 of `Dickinson_Slides.pptx` and save the file. Then extract all speaker notes from the updated file and save them to `notes.docx` on the Desktop.

I'd like to have those notes handy in a separate document when I rehearse. Could you assist me in extracting all the presenter notes from the Impress file and saving them as a Word document? Just keep the text of the notes, do not add any formatting or page number information. I'd like the file to be named 'notes.docx' and placed on my Desktop for easy access.

metadata.explanation: Chains two objectives: (1) add a note to the currently empty slide 7 and save the PPTX, (2) then extract all 9 notes (including the new one) to notes.docx. Partial credit: 0.5 for PPTX note updated, 0.5 for docx containing the new note. llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads slide 7 (index 6, 0-based) note text from the PPTX file using python-pptx, matching the instruction's target slide.
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (expected.get('slide7_note')) — proper handling for expected.type='rule' where framework passes rules dict directly.
Sub-goal 1 (PPTX note check) fully verified: checks that 'No content slide.' is contained in slide 7's note text with case-insensitive comparison.

Sub-goal 2 (docx presence check) partially verified: confirms the new note appears somewhere in notes.docx, but does NOT verify that all speaker notes (all 9 slides) were extracted — instruction says 'extract ALL speaker notes'.
Both getters read saved files (not UI state), so no postconfig is needed.
Negative control resistance is adequate: do-nothing agent scores 0.0 (no PPTX note, no docx).
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To fully verify 'extract ALL speaker notes', add a check in the metric or getter that counts or compares all expected note lines (e.g., verify docx_lines contains notes from all 9 slides, not just the new slide 7 note). This prevents passing an agent that saves only a single-line docx.
